rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without excessive risk of truncation. This should reveal whether peaks are compressed early, held to the final hold, or spread across the gradient for targeted refinement next.

All compounds eluted well within the gradient, so trim the gradient window to the observed elution region to concentrate gradient time where the peaks are and reduce total run time. The estimated elution range is roughly phi_e 0.11 to 0.59, so 0.20–0.60 should keep late peaks in-gradient while avoiding wasted strong-solvent range.

The trimmed window was too weak and too slow, pushing the first peak near dead time and the last peak much later; the sweet spot is likely a somewhat narrower but still stronger window than the scout, with a shorter gradient to cut time. This run tests whether keeping roughly the same elution region but increasing slope can preserve resolution while improving CRF.

The current best is very fast but the 6/7 pair is just below baseline resolution, so make the gradient slightly shallower while keeping the same phi window. If that pair responds to slope, this should lift its resolution above 1.5 with only a small time penalty.

The 6/7 pair clearly responds to slope, but the 10 min run is already near-optimal on time, so test temperature as a finer selectivity lever while keeping the best fast gradient. A modest increase to 45 C may reorder or spread the critical middle pair enough to retain the zero time penalty and improve the resolution term to 1.000.

Temperature worsened the critical pair, so return to 40 C and adjust the phi window instead. A slightly higher phi1 should shift the middle-to-late compounds to a different part of the gradient and may improve the 6/7 selectivity while keeping the run in the zero time-penalty region.

Probe the other side of the phi-window around the current best: lowering phi1 slightly may move the critical 6/7 pair to a more favorable composition region while still keeping all compounds in-gradient and within the no-time-penalty range. This tests whether selectivity around that pair is maximized below the 0.65 endpoint.

Changing phi1 showed the 6/7 pair is sensitive to conditions, and a lower endpoint improved its resolution at the cost of time; now test temperature in the opposite direction from the failed 45 C run. A drop to 35 C may improve selectivity for the critical pair while still keeping the run close to the no-time-penalty region.

Temperature changes hurt selectivity, so keep 40 C and adjust the starting composition instead. Raising phi0 slightly may reposition the crowded mid-eluting cluster within the gradient while preserving the favorable endpoint, potentially improving the critical spacing without much effect on run time.

You have already reached the maximum CRF, so the best strategic move is to confirm whether a nearby method offers more robustness around the critical 6/7 pair while staying at the same optimum score. Increasing phi0 one more step tests whether the selectivity improvement continues or if the first peak starts becoming too close to unretained.

The optimum score persists and the critical pair keeps improving as phi0 increases, so continue one more step to probe robustness while staying in the zero time-penalty regime. This tests the limit before the earliest peak approaches the dead-time region too closely.

The best region appears centered near phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.60–0.65; since higher phi0 beyond 0.15 started to hurt the critical pair, now test a slightly lower phi1 combined with the stronger phi0 0.15. This may preserve the improved early-peak spacing while nudging the 6/7 pair to even safer resolution, still with no time penalty.

The optimum sits on a ridge around phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.65, so test the complementary corner by increasing phi1 while keeping the successful phi0 0.10. This checks whether the maximum is broad in endpoint composition or whether 0.65 is the true local optimum.

With CRF already at the maximum, the only remaining opportunity is to see whether an even shorter gradient still preserves full resolution and thus also scores 1.000. Using the current best composition window, reduce tG to 8 min to test the lower edge of the optimum time plateau.

The 8 min gradient was too steep at phi0 0.10, but phi0 0.15 gave slightly stronger robustness at 10 min; test whether that higher start can rescue the critical 6/7 pair at the shorter gradient. This maps whether the zero-time-penalty optimum extends to 8 min in a narrower part of composition space.

The composition optimum is already established, so use a remaining shot to map temperature more fully around the best method. Since 35 C and 45 C both degraded selectivity, 30 C tests whether the effect is monotonic or if there is a lower-temperature selectivity window that could also sustain a maximum score.

The maximum-score region is clearly near 40 C and tG 10, with best robustness around phi0 0.10–0.15 and phi1 0.65; this untested neighbor checks whether the second optimum at phi0 0.15 extends to a slightly higher endpoint. It helps define the breadth of the plateau around the best methods without revisiting known poor directions.

Both best methods are already at CRF 1.000, so use a remaining run to probe robustness in a slower, slightly weaker-window direction that may further increase the minimum resolution if the scoring plateau is broad. This checks whether a composition near the optimum but with slightly shallower slope can still stay on the maximum-CRF plateau.

The 40 C, 10 min, 0.10–0.65 method is already optimal, but 45 C caused a severe selectivity collapse and it is useful to define whether that was a local effect or part of a broader high-temperature failure. Testing 50 C maps the upper-temperature boundary of the optimum region while keeping all other factors fixed.

The best zone is tightly centered at 40 C, but since phi0 0.15 gave a co-optimal method at 40 C, test whether that slightly stronger starting composition is more temperature-robust at 45 C than phi0 0.10. This explores whether the 45 C selectivity collapse can be mitigated by composition near the second optimum.

The remaining useful information is the temperature robustness boundary of the optimal composition; 45 and 50 C were both poor, so 55 C will confirm whether high temperature uniformly collapses the same critical pair. This cleanly brackets the optimum around 40 C while avoiding any repeat of prior methods.

55 C unexpectedly restores full performance for the phi0 0.10 optimum, so the most informative next step is to test whether the co-optimal phi0 0.15 method also lies on this high-temperature maximum plateau. This will define whether the best region is broad in both phi0 and temperature, giving a more robust final recommendation.

55 C appears beneficial only in part of the composition space, so test whether lowering phi0 restores or improves robustness at the same fast endpoint and gradient time. This explores the interaction between start composition and the surprising high-temperature optimum without repeating any prior condition.

Two methods already achieve the maximum score, and 55 C looks promising with phi0 0.10; lowering phi1 slightly may improve the minimum resolution while likely remaining in the zero-time-penalty region. This is a targeted final refinement around the high-temperature optimum.

For the final injection, bracket the high-temperature optimum by testing the opposite endpoint direction from injection 24. This determines whether the 55 C maximum-score region is centered specifically at phi1 0.65 or remains broad across 0.60–0.70 while keeping the proven optimal phi0 and tG.
